subsystems.name: Stimulus delivery
subsystems.role: presents a specific visual or auditory prompt at a precisely known time.

subsystems.name: EEG sensing
subsystems.role: picks up the tiny voltage changes on the scalp that reflect neural activity.

subsystems.name: Signal conditioning
subsystems.role: removes noise and artefacts so the neural response can be isolated.

subsystems.name: Feature extraction
subsystems.role: turns the cleaned signal into numbers that differ between people.

subsystems.name: Classification model
subsystems.role: decides whether the response matches the enrolled user.

subsystems.name: Security integration
subsystems.role: connects the neural check to an access-control system without leaking biometric data.

buildSteps.title: Collect reference data
buildSteps.detail: Record EEG responses from many volunteers to the same stimulus to learn how much individuals differ and how stable each person is over time.

buildSteps.title: Design the stimulus
buildSteps.detail: Choose a prompt (for example a flickering image or a tone) that reliably evokes a measurable, person-specific neural response.

buildSteps.title: Build the recording rig
buildSteps.detail: Assemble a comfortable headset with dry electrodes and a low-noise amplifier, aiming for a setup a non-expert can put on in under a minute.

buildSteps.title: Clean the signal
buildSteps.detail: Develop filters and algorithms that remove eye blinks, muscle movement and mains interference without erasing the neural response.

buildSteps.title: Extract features
buildSteps.detail: Compute compact numerical descriptors from the response, such as ERP amplitudes and latencies or spectral power in chosen bands.

buildSteps.title: Train the classifier
buildSteps.detail: Use the features to train a model that separates the enrolled user from impostors, validating with data recorded on different days.

buildSteps.title: Test robustness
buildSteps.detail: Measure how accuracy changes with electrode position, hair type, fatigue, caffeine and background noise.

buildSteps.title: Probe for spoofing
buildSteps.detail: Try to defeat the system with recorded signals or synthetic EEG to see whether liveness checks are needed.

buildSteps.title: Integrate and pilot
buildSteps.detail: Connect the prototype to a door or workstation and run it in a controlled high-security setting.

prerequisites.why: research-grade caps are bulky and need gel; comfortable dry sensors are improving but still less stable.
everyday movement and eye blinks easily swamp the tiny neural signal.
standard classifiers can learn individual patterns once clean features are available.
neural templates must be stored and compared without being stolen or replayed.
people may resist wearing a headset for routine access, and no common protocol exists.

pathway.milestone: research studies showing that EEG responses to a stimulus can distinguish individuals with high accuracy in the lab
pathway.unlocks: proof that the concept is physically possible.

pathway.milestone: comfortable headset prototypes tested outside the lab, over weeks, with many users
pathway.unlocks: evidence that the signal is stable enough for real use.

pathway.milestone: pilots in high-security access control alongside fingerprints or tokens
pathway.unlocks: real-world data on reliability, spoofing and user experience.

pathway.milestone: integration into consumer or workplace devices with dedicated low-power EEG sensors
pathway.unlocks: neural response as one factor in a multi-factor authentication scheme.
